title: The Rook
subtitle: Straight lines, long range — meet your heavy piece.
goals: Move the rook along ranks and files

steps.say: This is the rook. It moves in straight lines — forward, backward, and sideways — as far as it wants, as long as nothing is in the way.
Watch how much of the board one rook can cover.

autoMoves.say: Along the whole rank in a single move...
...and straight up the file. On an open board the rook is a monster.

steps.prompt: Capture the black pawn with your rook.
hints: The rook moves in straight lines. Is the pawn on the same file as your rook?
Slide the rook straight up the d-file.

line.say: Exactly! The pawn was on the rook's file, so it was just one slide away.

steps.wrongSay: The rook only moves in straight lines — look for a rank or file that leads to the pawn.
steps.successSay: Nice capture. Rooks punish anything left on their lines.

steps.prompt: Capture all three black pawns — one rook move at a time.
hints: Plan a route: after each capture, which pawn shares a line with your rook?
Start with the pawn straight up the d-file, then slide across.

sequenceGoal.say: Good — keep going, the rook's route continues!

steps.wrongSay: That move doesn't capture anything. Find the pawn that sits on your rook's rank or file.
steps.successSay: All three! You just made the rook tour the board like a vacuum cleaner.

steps.prompt: Two pawns are on your rook's rank — but only one is safe to take. Capture it!
hints: Before you capture, ask: can anything take my rook back?
The b4 pawn is guarded by the pawn on a5. The h4 pawn has no friends nearby.

line.say: Correct — the h-pawn was undefended, so the rook grabs it for free.

rejections.say: The a5 pawn recaptures your rook! Trading a rook for a pawn is a terrible deal. Look for the pawn nobody defends.

steps.wrongSay: You can capture a pawn this move — pick the one that can't be taken back.
steps.successSay: That's the golden rule of captures: free stuff first, guarded stuff never (unless it's worth it).

hints: Your king already stops the black king from stepping forward. Which line can the rook seal off?
Slide the rook to the back rank — the king will have nowhere left to go.

line.say: Checkmate! The rook covers the whole back rank, and your king guards every escape square in front.

rejections.say: Close — but the king simply slips to d8 or f8. Cut off the back rank itself.

steps.wrongSay: Not mate yet — the king still has an escape square. Which rank does he live on?
steps.successSay: Your first rook checkmate — the back-rank pattern will win you countless games.
